title: RBI Governor Tightens Rules for Online Lending Platforms
description: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das recently announced new guidelines for Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending platforms. These platforms connect individuals who want to lend .

faq.q: What kind of loans can I get through P2P platforms?
faq.a: You can typically get unsecured personal loans, small business loans, or loans for specific purposes like education or medical emergencies.

faq.q: Are there limits to how much I can lend or borrow?
faq.a: Yes, the RBI has set limits. For an individual, the aggregate exposure (total amount lent across all P2P platforms) to all borrowers at any point in time cannot exceed ₹50 lakh. Similarly, there are limits on how much an individual can borrow.

faq.q: What happens if a borrower doesn't repay?
faq.a: The P2P platform usually has a loan recovery process, which might include reminders, collection agents, or legal action, as per their terms and conditions. The new guidelines aim to make these processes more transparent.

Yes, platforms typically charge fees to both lenders and borrowers for their services, such as origination fees for borrowers or service fees for lenders. The new rules emphasize transparency in these charges.
